approved_scope: Stateless internal comparison of typed C12 vulnerability reports and C19 passport evidence references. New vulnerability findings and removed evidence are independent outputs. No file-byte verification, report/passport binding, trust, persistence, CLI or UI.
source_identity_method: SHA-256 over sorted relative-path + NUL + raw per-file SHA-256 digest records.
source_identity_scope: 529 tracked/nonignored source, tests, configs, locks and documentation files; excludes docs/evidence/, plans/progress.json, plans/requirements.json, plans/project-state.json, docs/agents/SESSION_HANDOFF.json, apps/web/src/generated/project.json and SHA256SUMS.txt. Ignored dependency/build/cache outputs excluded by git.

results.acceptance: New findings are identified by vulnerability ID, package name and package version. Removed passport evidence is identified by path and digest. The two result lists are independent, retain first-seen input order, and deduplicate matching identities.
results.negative_cases: Fixture tests cover either change alone, severity-only changes, package-version changes, digest changes at an unchanged path, and unchanged snapshots. The function is pure and has no source-execution or persistence path. Writer kill/replay/ACK/quota scenarios were excluded from C22 under the approved stateless scope.
results.security: The comparison consumes typed data only and leaves passport verification claims unchanged. It does not validate referenced bytes, prove that the supplied vulnerability report is bound to either passport, or establish signer trust.
results.regression: The complete Go suite, Go vet/build, and existing web checks passed. No database, migration, .env, Dockerfile, API, CLI, UI or dependency changes were made.
results.quality: go vet and go build passed. npm run check passed plan validation, TypeScript typecheck, production build and 28 Node tests. The project has no separate lint script.

limitations: C22 reports changes between caller-supplied typed claims; it does not verify passport digests, actual evidence bytes or correspondence between each Grype report and its passport.
The complete-engine hardware target and C30 workflow remain unverified; C28 owns workload measurement.
No remote CI, push or publication was performed.
